reported.title: pH conversion omits division by 500 mV/pH
reported.description: computePh() at line 23 simply returns the millivolt value unchanged, so the 500 mV/pH scaling is never applied. The measured output confirms this: at 9.01 s the firmware printed 4496.58 pH while the injected value was 8.7–9.02 pH, and the nominal ramp printed 5000 pH for a 10.0 pH input. The ADC-to-mV conversion at line 18 is correct, but the missing divide-by-500 in computePh() makes every printed value wrong. Firmware printed 4496.58 pH at 9.01 s while the injected input was 8.7 to 9.02 pH: off by 4487.6 pH (tolerance ±0.2). 9 of 9 values were wrong.

reported.title: Alert LED driven from unscaled millivolt value
reported.description: The alert comparison at line 66 tests lastPh (which is really millivolts, per the bug in computePh()) against ALERT_PH=7.20, so the LED threshold is effectively 7.2 mV rather than 7.2 pH. Measured evidence shows D13 not HIGH for 940 ms while required during the rail-saturation scenario and 500 ms during the glitch scenario. Because the reported value is ~500x too large, the LED is almost always LOW when it should be HIGH. D13 was in the wrong state for 427 ms across 364 interval(s), first at 512 ms: D13 was not HIGH for 1 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Linearized pH probe on A0 with scale 500 mV/pH (0 mV → pH 0.0); low-pH alert LED on D13.
- Convert ADC samples using a 5.000 V / 1023 full-scale span, then divide millivolts by 500 to obtain pH.
- Print exactly one line every 1000 ms matching `pH: <value>` with two decimal places.
- Printed pH must stay within ±0.20 of the injected probe value.
- Drive D13 HIGH when reported pH is below 7.20; otherwise drive D13 LOW.
- Keep logging while the alert LED is on or off.
